subject: Network pathing & streaming SLOs — post-call checklist
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Sierra Gomez <sierra@quantify.ai>, Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@quantify.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Network pathing & streaming SLOs — post-call checklist

Thanks for taking the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our call on private VPC connectivity and streaming SLOs. High level: Quantify AI wants to run low-latency streaming inference from a private deployment (VPC peering or VPN) with predictable tail latency and throughput for interactive product usage.

Key customer targets we captured on the call (confirm if any of these need correction):
- Primary SLOs: first-byte (stream start) P95 <= 120ms, end-to-end response P95 <= 450ms, P99 targets: first-byte <= 250ms.
- Throughput/concurrency: target steady-state ~220 concurrent user streams, peak bursts up to ~400 concurrent streams. Typical response size ~350 tokens; av. token generation rate ~35 tokens/sec.
- Network constraints: traffic egress through a single NAT IP/egress path; VPN tunnel (IPsec) only, no direct peering for now; egress cap ~1 Gbps with occasional spikes to 1.6 Gbps during batch imports.
- Failover: desire a fallback path off-hosted Redwood endpoints (not a hard requirement, just to understand options).

What we need from Quantify engineering to validate acceptance criteria and sizing for a Private deployment:
1) A small sample pcap or flow log showing RTT to your gateway and typical connection churn (you mentioned you can share exports).
2) A short list of expected request QPS and avg payload sizes per stream (we captured estimates above but would prefer precise numbers per region).
3) Confirmation if TLS termination is on your side (VPN) or if you expect Redwood to terminate TLS inside the private endpoint.
4) Any IP allowlist constraints (single egress IP, strict outbound port restrictions).

Next steps / owners:
- Alejandro: send pcap/throughput PDF and any firewall rules (by Tue, 2027-05-10).
- Monica (cc'd): we'll run an internal SLO-sizing pass once we have the pcap and exact concurrency distribution; she'll coordinate a sizing doc + recommended Dedicated config.
- Jonas: I'll loop you in for kernel/latency edge cases — mainly around streaming first-byte latency.

Attachments referenced: N/A in this message.

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
email: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai | mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@quantify.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Sierra Gomez <sierra@quantify.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network pathing & streaming SLOs — post-call checklist

Nikhil — thanks for the clear recap. Attached are two artifacts from our infra team: quantify-vpn-throughput-20270507.pdf (summary of measured throughput across our VPN concentrator over 72h) and network-trace-20270507.pcap (short 10-minute capture around a peak window). Note: both files contain internal IPs sanitized.

Quick clarifications / numbers: 
- Streaming requirements: our front-end opens persistent client streams; each stream is ~350 tokens on average. We currently see ~30–40 tokens/sec per stream when generating.
- Concurrency: typical steady concurrency ~180–240; we plan to support up to 420 concurrent streams during peak marketing events.
- Bandwidth: sustained ~600 Mbps during heavy periods; we see short spikes up to ~1.6 Gbps (roughly 30–90s).
- Latency observed to our gateway (internal): RTT to our exit gateway ~18–28ms normally; occasional spikes to 60–80ms during heavy egress.
- VPN: we have an IPsec tunnel (vendor: StratusVpn). We can open additional tunnels for redundancy but prefer to start with a single primary tunnel for now.
- Egress: everything exits from a known NAT IP range. We can provide the CIDR (will include in a follow-up email).

Two asks for Redwood:
A) Can Redwood confirm whether the first-byte streaming handoff introduces any additional tail latency given our topology (VPN -> Internet -> Redwood private endpoint)? We want to understand whether the P95 first-byte budget above is feasible without peering.
B) Sizing: a recommended Dedicated pool configuration (g1/g2 tier?) for our target concurrency and token rates — feel free to provide ranges.

I'll follow up by EOD Monday with the CIDR and the sanitized IKE logs.

Best,
Alejandro
Network Engineering — Quantify AI
--
[Attachment: quantify-vpn-throughput-20270507.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: network-trace-20270507.pcap (pcap)]
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@quantify.ai>, Sierra Gomez <sierra@quantify.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network pathing & streaming SLOs — post-call checklist

Appreciate the artifacts, Alejandro — those are exactly what we need. High-level reactions from our infra sizing pass (Monica & Jonas looped):
- Feasibility: with a 1 Gbps sustained ceiling we will need to recommend either (a) extra tunnels for redundancy/bandwidth aggregation, or (b) apply client-side rate limiting for worst-case marketing spikes. Spikes to 1.6 Gbps will oversubscribe a single 1G tunnel.
- Latency: VPN + Internet hop will add variance; from our internal measurements we can usually keep first-byte P95 <= 120ms if RTT from your gateway to our private endpoint stays < ~60ms and if packet loss is <0.5%. The spikes you observed to 60–80ms are near the limit — we should monitor.

Concrete asks to finalize sizing and an acceptance test plan:
1) Please provide a simple synthetic test harness (or confirm we can run a blue-green test) that opens N concurrent client streams and emits a fixed token-per-second profile. We’ll use this to validate first-byte and full-response SLOs over your VPN tunnel.
2) If you can provide expected concurrency distribution percentiles (p50,p75,p90,p95,p99) that will help pin autoscaling thresholds.
3) Confirm whether TLS is terminated on your side (you mentioned yes on the call) — if so we will validate TLS-over-VPN vs TLS-terminated-at-Redwood differences in the test.

Proposed acceptance tests (brief):
- Warm-up: 10 minutes at p50 load.
- Ramp to p95 steady state for 15 minutes and measure first-byte and P95/P99 end-to-end latency.
- Spike test: 90s burst to 1.5x peak to confirm graceful degradation and autoscaling behavior.

I'll draft a short test plan and recommended Dedicated pool options (3 sizing variants) and share by EOD Tuesday once we have the concurrency percentiles. Monica will own the sizing doc.

Thanks — looking forward to the p50/p95 numbers.

– Nikhil
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Sierra Gomez <sierra@quantify.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@quantify.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network pathing & streaming SLOs — post-call checklist

Nikhil / Monica — small update before Alejandro sends the CIDR. We dug into our usage telemetry and produced the concurrency percentiles you requested: p50=95, p75=165, p90=210, p95=310, p99=410. Token distribution per request: median 320, mean 355, 95th percentile 520.

We can run the synthetic harness you describe — Ops can coordinate a window next Wednesday (2027-05-12) in UTC morning. We'll confirm the exact test times after Alejandro posts the CIDR and IKE logs.

One additional note: we prefer Redwood to do the TLS termination inside the private endpoint (Redwood-managed certs are fine) — simplifies our key management. If that increases latency significantly compared to TLS termination on our side, call that out in the sizing doc.

Thanks,
Sierra
Head of Product — Quantify AI
